# Bankruptcy Appraiser (bankruptcy-appraiser.com)

> Real estate appraisals for Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcy cases in San Diego County and Riverside County, California, by Brian Ward, California Certified Residential Real Estate Appraiser since 2004. A website of Brian Ward Appraisal (https://www.brianward.com/).

Phone: (760) 557-2147. Email: contact@bankruptcy-appraiser.com. Office: 15877 Paseo Del Sur, San Diego, CA.

Starting fees: Basic Desktop $299; Desktop $449; Drive-By $649; Standard $699; Desktop 2-4 Unit $549; Standard 2-4 Unit $799. Written quote before work begins.

## Guides
- [Your Home and a Chapter 7 Filing: Where the Appraisal Fits](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/chapter-7/): In Chapter 7 the trustee asks one practical question about your house, and a credible appraisal is how you answer it.
- [Chapter 13 and Your Home: How an Appraisal Supports the Plan](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/chapter-13/): A Chapter 13 plan lets you keep the house, but the plan still has to account for what that house is worth.
- [The California Homestead Exemption and Why Value Drives It](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/homestead-exemption/): The exemption protects a slice of your home equity, and you cannot know whether it covers you until you know what the home is worth.
- [Valuing a Home as of the Petition Date](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/petition-date-value/): A bankruptcy appraisal often describes the market on a day that has already passed, and doing that well takes a specific method.
- [Appraisals for Chapter 13 Lien Stripping and Motions to Value](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/lien-stripping/): Whether a second mortgage survives a Chapter 13 case can come down to a few dollars of value, so the appraisal has to be built to withstand scrutiny.
- [Appraisal Support for Debtor Attorneys and Their Staff](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/for-attorneys/): A straightforward process for law offices that need defensible values on Schedule A/B, plan confirmation, and motions to value.
- [Independent Appraisals for Trustees and Creditors' Counsel](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/for-trustees/): When the value on a debtor's schedules needs a second look, an independent appraisal gives the estate a documented basis for its next step.
- [Rental Homes and 2-4 Unit Properties in a Bankruptcy Case](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/bankruptcy-guides/rentals-and-multi-unit/): Investment property is treated differently from the home you live in, and the appraisal has to reflect how buyers of rentals actually think.

## Reports
- [Bankruptcy Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/bankruptcy/): A defensible value for your home as of the petition date, written for Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 cases.
- [Date-of-Death Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/date-of-death/): A retrospective market value fixed to the day an owner passed, documented for tax and court use.
- [Divorce Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/divorce/): A neutral home value both spouses and their attorneys can rely on when dividing community property.
- [Estate & Trust Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/estate-trust/): Clear values for trustees and executors who must inventory, divide, sell or distribute real estate.
- [Expert Witness Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/expert-witness/): Litigation-ready appraisals and clear testimony from a certified appraiser with two decades of local work.
- [Family Transfer Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/family-transfer/): A documented value when a home passes between parents, children, siblings or other relatives.
- [Immigration I-864 Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/immigration-i864/): Documented home equity for sponsors who use real estate as an asset on the Affidavit of Support.
- [Insurance Claim Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/insurance-claim/): Market value evidence before and after damage, for homeowners and attorneys working through a property claim.
- [Pre-Listing Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/pre-listing/): An independent value before you list, so the price starts from evidence rather than optimism.
- [Pre-Purchase Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/pre-purchase/): An independent check on price before you commit, especially when no lender will order an appraisal.
- [Property Tax Appeal Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/tax-appeal/): Evidence for a decline-in-value review or assessment appeal, built around the January 1 lien date.
- [Bail Bond Property Appraisal](https://www.bankruptcy-appraiser.com/reports/bail-bond/): A quick, well-supported value for a family home being put up as collateral for a bail bond or property bond.
